GlobalGoogle Antigravity for science: 10,000 researchers get the highest usage tier free for six months, with Gemini 4 Argon

≈$300

FreeAt the Gemini 4 Argon launch Google offered 10,000 scientists six months of Antigravity's highest usage tier plus Gemini 4 Argon at no cost. Ongoing ·For non-commercial researchers affiliated with a university, degree-granting institution, non-profit institute or national laboratory. AI Tools & CreditsFreeVerified
Actual value≈$300 · 6 months of the top usage tier
What you get
Google Antigravity is Google's agent-first development environment, where several agents work in parallel on a desktop app. When Gemini 4 Argon launched on 13 October 2026, Google opened a science programme alongside it: up to 10,000 researchers get six months of Antigravity's highest usage tier and Gemini 4 Argon free of charge. An ordinary individual needs the Google AI Ultra subscription at $249.99 a month to use Argon in Antigravity, so the grant is worth half a year at that level. Applications go through an interest form behind Apply for free access on antigravity.google/use-cases/science: sign in with the Google account you want upgraded, give your institution, institutional email and a public lab or personal page, add an ORCID or Google Scholar profile (one of the two), and write a short summary of the research you plan over the next 6 to 12 months. Google stores the summary with the application and asks that it be non-confidential and non-proprietary. Review is rolling and weekly, subject to capacity. On 10 November Google noted more than 27,000 applications since 13 October with roughly 3,000 admitted so far, and only selected applicants are contacted. Once selected, the account is upgraded and the Science plugin installs in one click from the in-app Customizations marketplace, giving agents direct access to 30-plus life-science databases including the AlphaGenome Atlas, AlphaFold Database, UniProt, PubChem and ChEMBL. The form is not limited to life sciences: medicine, chemistry and materials, physics and fusion, quantum computing, climate, neuroscience, mathematics, computer science, engineering, social sciences, agriculture and economics are all listed, as long as the work is non-commercial.
Conditions
Non-commercial research only; an active affiliation at a university, degree-granting institution, non-profit research institute or national laboratory (faculty, postdocs, staff scientists, research engineers, PhD and master's students; no dedicated option for undergraduates); at least one of ORCID or Google Scholar; institution, institutional email, public page and a 6-12 month research summary without confidential or unpublished data; up to 10,000 places with rolling review, and only selected applicants are contacted; the upgrade applies to the Google account used to apply.

Steps
  1. Sign in with the Google account you want upgraded at antigravity.google/use-cases/science
  2. Click Apply for free access and fill in institution, institutional email and a public page
  3. Add an ORCID or Google Scholar link and a 6-12 month research summary
  4. Submit and wait for rolling review; selected applicants are notified and the account is upgraded
  5. Install the Science plugin from Antigravity's Customizations marketplace
The 10,000 places are a ceiling, not a promise: Google reported about 3,000 admitted from over 27,000 applications by 10 November, fewer than one in nine; the top tier has no published quota, so heavy multi-agent work may still hit limits; the programme says nothing about what happens after six months, so do not rest a project on it; the research summary is stored by Google, so keep it non-confidential; the upgrade belongs to the individual account, not an institution.

What you get
Upsolve (YC W24) builds an analytics agent for your data warehouse: ask in plain English why revenue dropped last quarter and it writes the SQL, draws the charts and writes up the answer, and it can save results into Notion or open a Linear ticket. The official pricing page lists a Free plan at $0 with 1,000 one-time credits (roughly 500 analytical questions), no credit card, then $0.10 per credit, or the Team plan at $160/month billed annually with 5,000 credits a month. Credit costs vary by work: a clarification is under 1 credit, a basic data lookup 0.5–1, a full analytical question 1–3, and building dashboards or data apps 10–50 — so the allowance goes much further on questions than on dashboards. The Free plan still includes the AI analyst, agentic dashboards and presentations, the data model, skills and knowledge base, the playground, the CLI and the remote MCP server (https://mcp.upsolve.ai/mcp), and bring-your-own-key through Upsolve Local. Row-level security, embedding and team features are Team-only. The CLI runs with npx @upsolve-labs/analytics.
Conditions
Register an account (18+). The 1,000 Free credits are one-time, not monthly. You need to connect your own data source for it to do anything useful. Row-level security/RBAC, embedding and multi-tenant features are Team-only. Data is processed in the US and UK, so do not upload regulated or confidential data. When the credits run out you pay $0.10 per credit or upgrade.

  4. To use it inside Claude, Cursor or Codex, add the remote MCP server https://mcp.upsolve.ai/mcp under Settings → Connectors and sign in with the same account

What you get
This is an official LinkedIn and Lovable perk rather than a third-party coupon: Lovable's offer page states that LinkedIn Premium members get 12 months of Lovable Pro Lite plus 300 credits granted at activation. Pro Lite carries all standard Pro features but a different credit model, only 5 bonus credits a day instead of Pro's monthly allowance, so heavy use means buying credits. Redemption has to go through LinkedIn: sign in, open the Premium perks page, find the Lovable card and follow it into Lovable to activate. The codes are single-use and non-transferable. LinkedIn's help centre adds that the benefit cannot be redeemed on an iOS device, so use a desktop browser regardless of where the subscription was bought; it is for the primary account holder only; Premium Company Page subscribers do not qualify; and free-trial members must finish the trial and make a first payment before redeeming. Both sides have to qualify: a paid LinkedIn Premium in one of the four countries, and a new or free Lovable workspace, since accounts already on a paid plan are excluded. In June 2026 Lovable's growth lead said the 300-credit perk had opened globally to Premium members, yet the official page still described a four-country launch with more regions to come when checked in October, so treat the card in your own perks page as the deciding evidence.
Conditions
A paid LinkedIn Premium subscription (free trials must convert and make a first payment) with the LinkedIn account in the US, UK, Canada or Australia; redeem only through LinkedIn's Premium perks page and never on an iOS device; primary account holder only, not Premium Company Page subscribers; the Lovable workspace must be new or free, with paid workspaces excluded; codes are single-use and non-transferable; Pro Lite grants 5 bonus credits a day rather than Pro's monthly credits.

What you get
Articul8, backed by Intel, launched Bivia on 28 October 2026 as a compact multimodal decision model: it reads text, images, documents, code, signals and audio-video, then returns one structured judgement across nine decision types (choice, boolean, score, set, span, ground, extract, data science and more) with a real confidence score, and can abstain when the evidence is too thin. Pricing is $0.042 per million input tokens with output billed at zero, which suits the many small calls an agent makes, routing, triage and yes/no questions, while the large model handles the writing. It plugs in through a single HTTP POST with the same JSON every time, Python, Node, Go and Rust SDKs, an MCP server for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and VS Code, a floating macOS and Windows app, a Chrome and Edge extension, and a =BIVIA.DECIDE formula in Google Sheets. The launch offer gives the first 10,000 early adopters up to 1 billion tokens free with no subscription: claim from articul8.ai/bivia or the registration link carrying the Bivia code, then create an API key. At $0.042 a million input tokens, a billion tokens is roughly $42 of usage; how much actually lands and how long it lasts are not stated on the page, and community reports suggest about 90 days, so check the account balance. It is not a chat model: ask it for prose and it will not deliver, because it only answers in fixed decision shapes.

What you get
make.fun is a skill-based competition platform where AI agents build software for cash: each bounty states what to build, its reward and the metric it ranks on, and entrants use their own coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot or anything else) to build the work, then submit a public repository at one fixed commit plus the AI session transcripts that produced it. Automatic checks confirm the transcripts match the code, and a grader runs every entry the same way twice in a sandbox and ranks them on the published metric. Money and settlement: each bounty's reward is locked in an on-chain escrow on Solana, with source at github.com/makefunai/prize-escrow so anyone can check the on-chain program against the code. Ranked winners claim from the escrow to their own wallet and the platform does not push payments; a few earlier bounties without an escrow are paid from make.fun's reward wallet and say so on the page. Officially, from 9 November 2026 make.fun has paid $5,967.50 in USDC to 413 accounts, each with a Solana transaction signature on record. Free and costs: almost every bounty is free to enter, with no payment and no stake; a bounty with an entry fee says so and the fee goes into that bounty's pool. The real cost is your time and model calls, since the agent spends your own account's quota unless the bounty issues a sponsor-funded build key. The 18 November change, from the official X account @makefunai: you no longer have to win to get paid. Finishing in the top 1,000 without taking a paid place splits an extra participation pool, more for a better finish; amounts are usually under a cent but stack across contests, the balance shows at the top of the site, and once it reaches $0.25 you press Claim and it goes to your Solana wallet in USDC. What is live on 21 November 2026, with bounties opening and closing constantly: $35 poems and jokes, $50 spot-the-difference and poster art, $100 to $250 news images and data forecasts, $250 GTA 6 cover art and trophy guides, $500 video clipping or a 4KB Python chess engine, $1,000 for Bring the humans again, $1,325 for a token launch radar and $1,666 for Make GTA 6, alongside tasks that need a public X account or a YouTube channel. The platform's own wording matters: a bounty is a competition, not a wage. Only the listed paid places earn anything, an entry outside them earns nothing, and make.fun promises no amount, so never value it at the headline reward.

What you get
Checked on Quppy's official site (Personal page reviewed 2026-08-10, Help Center 2026-08-21, fees page 2026-08-26): - Entity: QUPPY EUROPE OU (Estonian registry code 14418677) provides only the technology and app and states plainly that it is not a bank. The fiat account is provided by a payment provider, and the current terms name 2PAYAPP LIMITED for euro SEPA processing. Inside the EEA, crypto custody and exchange are provided by Payhound Limited, a Malta-based MiCA-authorised CASP; outside the EEA the applicable licensed provider for the user's market applies, and Quppy does not name it. - IBAN: the personal multicurrency IBAN uses one set of account details for both EUR and GBP. Quppy's own support article gives the standard example GB12CLJU98523412345678 (GB, BIC CLJU, six-digit sort code 985234 and eight-digit account number 12345678), which is the "GB-prefixed UK IBAN" people refer to. Euros move over SEPA Standard and SEPA Instant, sterling over Faster Payments and CHAPS. - Current limits: incoming GBP transfers are not available, bank-card funding and payouts to bank cards are not available, and USD, local European IBANs and Solana are all marked coming soon. The Quppy card is marked coming soon. - Fees: the official fees page states the Quppy transfer fee on supported EUR and GBP transfers is EUR 0 / GBP 0 and opening an IBAN is free; exchange, blockchain network and third-party costs are separate, Quppy publishes no single exchange fee and the quote in the app prevails. A legacy support fee page also lists a 1.12% high-risk transaction fee, 2.1% for EUR to GBP and back, a 50 EUR/GBP compliance fee when KYC documents are not supplied in time, and a 5 EUR/GBP dormant-account fee per calendar month after 183 days without a transaction. - Crypto: a custodial wallet supporting BTC, ETH, TRON (TRX), USDC and USDT. USDT on Ethereum and TRON is explicitly unavailable to EEA users and available outside the EEA, which includes China; SOL and USDC/USDT on Solana are coming soon. The availability directory on the official site (status per country, last reviewed 2026-08-11) shows, for China as an individual: multicurrency IBAN in EUR and GBP available, crypto wallets and exchange available (outside MiCA), local payment methods available, local European IBANs not available, Quppy cards coming soon. For the United Kingdom every one of those five lines reads not available, and several people who signed up say not to select the UK as residence or nationality. On the card: Quppy lists the Quppy card (virtual and physical) as coming soon, says issuer, card type, fees and launch countries will be published before launch, and currently offers only an email waitlist, stating that joining the waitlist is not an application. User reports (many posted 2026-11-22): a Chinese ID card or passport passes KYC (Sumsub captures the document and selfie), the address is self-declared with no overseas proof of address required, and a mainland phone number works. The app is not in the mainland China or US App Store, so an Apple ID from another region or the Android APK from the official site is needed. Some users deposit 20 pounds into Wise through Quppy to activate it, but whether Wise accepts it has never been promised by Quppy.
Conditions
You must be 18 or older and pass KYC in the app: front and back of a passport or ID card (name in Latin letters) plus a selfie holding the document; user reports confirm a Chinese ID card and a mainland phone number work, with a self-declared address and no overseas proof of address. Do not give the United Kingdom as residence or nationality, because the official availability directory shows every service as unavailable there. The app is listed only in some App Store regions (not mainland China or the US); Android users can download the APK from the official site, and web access is not open yet. Incoming GBP, bank-card funding and payouts to bank cards are unavailable, so funding must come by bank transfer in EUR or GBP or in crypto. The Quppy card is not live and only a waitlist is open. Services and limits differ by country and the in-app configuration governs; passing KYC does not guarantee an approved account.
Countries & regions
[Global] Quppy says it serves eligible users worldwide except sanctioned or restricted jurisdictions, but availability is decided per country of residence: China (individual) shows the IBAN, crypto wallet and local payment methods as available, the United Kingdom shows everything unavailable, and Hong Kong and the Philippines work according to user reports. The IBAN is a GB-prefixed UK IBAN, but Quppy is not a bank
Starts & ends
Not announced → Ongoing / not announced
Official link
https://quppy.com/en/personal
Steps
  1. Download the app from quppy.com (iOS needs an Apple ID from another region, Android can use the APK from the official site), register with an email and set a four-digit PIN
  2. In Verification, enter name, gender and phone number, choose an ID card or passport, photograph both sides and take a selfie holding it, and enter your real address
  3. After approval open the IBAN account, tap Receive, and note the GB-prefixed IBAN with its six-digit sort code and eight-digit account number
  4. Fund it from a bank account in your own name in EUR or GBP, or create a USDT wallet (TRC-20 or ERC-20), withdraw USDT from an exchange and exchange it to EUR or GBP in the app
  5. For the card, leave your email on the waitlist at quppy.com/en/personal/card and wait for the official launch in your market
Quppy is not a bank; the IBAN is provided by a payment partner and is not covered by deposit insurance. The company is Estonian, EEA crypto services run through Payhound and non-EEA crypto through an unnamed local licensed provider, so the route to remedy a problem is long. Published fee figures disagree (Quppy publishes no exchange fee, a legacy support page says 2.1%, users quote 1.5%; for the dormant fee both 5 and 100 EUR/GBP circulate), so the in-app quote and terms govern. The dormant-account fee starts 183 days after the last transaction and keeps charging monthly. Crypto funding carries blockchain and compliance risk, large amounts can trigger source-of-funds questions, and this is not a place to park savings. Using the GB IBAN to activate Wise is a user claim that Wise has never promised to accept. The card is not launched, so any claim that it can be opened now is false or third-party. The app is not in the mainland China App Store and switching store regions carries its own risk; when verifying with an ID card, a polyphonic surname is romanised from the document and can end up differently from what you expect, in which case a passport is the alternative.

GlobalDigitalPlat FreeDomain: free .dpdns.org and .qzz.io names, ready for Cloudflare

≈$10

FreeThe non-profit DigitalPlat gives away second-level domains: .dpdns.org, .qzz.io and .qd.je cost nothing to register or renew, and you delegate the NS records to Cloudflare to run DNS yourself; registration needs real WHOIS details and GitHub verification, with one domain per account by default

Ongoing ·Registered at dash.domain.digitalplat.org with no host lock-in and DNS delegated to Cloudflare or your own authoritative server; real name, address, phone and email are required OfficialOfficial
Global VPS & CloudFreeVerified
Actual value≈$10 · Free subdomain
What you get
DigitalPlat FreeDomain is an open-source (AGPL-3.0) free public domain service for individuals and projects, with a GitHub repository in the hundreds of thousands of stars and an official README claiming more than 500,000 domains registered. It is free to register and free to renew rather than free for a first year, and the listed suffixes are .dpdns.org, .us.kg, .qzz.io, .xx.kg and .qd.je. What matters: it only handles name registration and NS delegation (bring your own DNS), while A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT and MX records live in Cloudflare or your own authoritative DNS. The typical flow is to add the full domain in Cloudflare first and note its two name servers, then enter the prefix, pick a suffix, paste the name servers and confirm the policies in the DigitalPlat dashboard, and finally add DNS records in Cloudflare once it is live. The gates: registration asks for a real name, email, phone and contact address, with WHOIS possibly public unless you enable privacy protection, and needs GitHub-based verification. Each account gets one domain by default, and the official FAQ says starring the repository is not required. Whether a given suffix is free must be confirmed in the dashboard, since third-party guides disagree about .us.kg and .xx.kg. Renewal happens within 180 days before expiry and is free. What it suits: personal homepages, portfolios, GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages and Vercel demos, API demos, temporary test environments, and learning DNS and SSL. What it does not suit: a commercial site or a single brand entry point. The project runs on donations, so suffix policies, quotas and upstream relationships can change; free suffixes carry weak reputation, so mail and ad network reviews get stricter; and control ultimately stays with the operator.
Conditions
Register a DigitalPlat account with real WHOIS details and complete GitHub-based verification; one free domain per account by default, with quota and suffix availability set by the dashboard; external authoritative name servers such as Cloudflare's two are required; registration and renewal are free, with the renewal window in the 180 days before expiry; phishing and spam are prohibited and abusive domains are reclaimed.
Countries & regions

  2. Register at dash.domain.digitalplat.org with your real name, email, phone and address, and complete GitHub verification
  3. Under Domain Registration enter the prefix, choose a suffix such as .dpdns.org, paste Cloudflare's name servers and submit
  4. After the NS delegation goes live add A or CNAME records in Cloudflare, and renew free in the dashboard within 180 days of expiry

Global eSIM GuideDeposit req.Verified
Actual value≈$8 · EUR 3 starter (EUR 3 back as credit); about EUR 8 a year to keep
What you get
A1 Hrvatska is the Croatian arm of Austria's A1 Group. Its official SIM-promo page sells a prepaid eSIM for EUR 3: choose eSIM, enter an email address and contact details, pay online and the QR code arrives immediately by email; scan it, finish online activation and you hold a +385 number. The EUR 3 returns as account credit, as the official terms state that registering your details earns EUR 3. The same page offers a free physical SIM, but it ships only inside Croatia, so the eSIM is the only cloud-activated route. Validity follows the official Uvjeti korištenja A1 usluge na bonove in force since 1 December 2025: a new card is valid 180 days, then each top-up adds days by amount - EUR 2-14 gives 92 days, EUR 15-29 gives 120, EUR 30-49 gives 180 and EUR 50-100 gives 360. Four minimum top-ups of EUR 2 cover about a year for roughly EUR 8, while a single EUR 50 top-up buys 360 days. After expiry a 270-day rescue window follows in which the number can only receive calls and SMS; one top-up inside it restores the line, and only after 270 days is the number closed. Roaming and codes: A1's roaming partner list names China Mobile and China Unicom (4G/LTE) for mainland China, and the official roaming guide states that received SMS are not charged, so verification codes need no data package. With no balance left the line can still receive calls and texts, which suits it as a pure code-receiving card. VoWiFi is closed to prepaid: A1 support confirmed in writing that VoLTE is disabled on prepaid lines for marketing reasons, and VoWiFi exists only on business tariffs. Caveats: ordering needs no passport upload (community tests through 2026), yet Croatian law does require prepaid users to be registered, so the details actually requested on the order page govern; payment needs a Visa or Mastercard that passes international checks; and the EUR 3 refund is a webshop promotion that may end at any time.
Conditions
Order the eSIM on the official SIM-promo page for EUR 3 with the QR code and number delivered by email and the EUR 3 returned as credit; outside Croatia only the eSIM is available (physical SIM ships inside Croatia only); validity per official terms: 180 days on activation, then 92 days for a EUR 2-14 top-up, 120 days for EUR 15-29, 180 days for EUR 30-49 and 360 days for EUR 50-100, with a 270-day window after expiry to top up and keep the number; the phone must support eSIM and be carrier unlocked; payment needs an international card.

Global eSIM GuideDeposit req.Verified
Actual value≈$6 · HKD 50 card, HKD 50 credit
What you get
haha SIM is the recyclable travel prepaid card from Hutchison (3HK) sold with Fortress, and it is the usual alternative to Club SIM: same +852 number and same no monthly fee, cheaper because the card arrives loaded, more awkward because there is no eSIM. The card costs about HKD 50 at Fortress and carries HKD 50 of credit, so the SIM itself is effectively free. The box prints a last activation date and the card is void after it. Once activated the balance reads about HKD 50, though a charge of about HKD 3.5 for an SMS can appear first. Keep-alive follows the Fortress terms: the number is valid 365 days from activation, and one top-up of at least HKD 10 in the haha TRAVEL app every 12 months extends it another 365 days from the top-up date. Two traps: buying a data pack does not count, only a top-up does, and the app's lowest top-up is often HKD 20, so an exact HKD 10 top-up goes through the 3HK prepaid top-up page, which accepts WeChat Pay and Alipay from the mainland. A card expired by less than 14 days can be restored on request without guarantee and needs registration again; later than that the number is gone. In the mainland it is a receiver: incoming SMS is free, while outgoing SMS costs HKD 3.5, incoming calls HKD 8 a minute, calls to Hong Kong HKD 8 a minute and calls to the mainland HKD 6 a minute. Data comes from day passes bought in the app, commonly HKD 10 a day with about 500MB at full speed. Registration is only compulsory for Hong Kong local service, so a card used purely for roaming codes can stay unregistered; the community also reports that buying one mainland day pass on a new card makes third-party codes arrive more reliably, which the vendor does not state. Community reports from September to November 2026: numbers are assigned at random and cannot be chosen or changed; the vendor sells no eSIM, and forcing a conversion on iPhone leaves haha TRAVEL unable to log in, so topping up and buying data stop working. WeChat and WhatsApp codes usually arrive, while Telegram and Google have many recent failures, which is a number-range and platform risk-control matter.
Conditions
Buy the physical card at Fortress or through 3HK for about HKD 50 with the same credit inside, and activate it before the last activation date printed on the box. Keep the number by topping up at least HKD 10 in the haha TRAVEL app or on the 3HK prepaid page every 12 months; buying data packs does not count. Only Hong Kong local service needs registration, and mainland roaming does not. No eSIM is offered, so the phone needs an unlocked physical SIM slot.

What you get
dtcpay is a Singapore-licensed payment institution (MAS Major Payment Institution, plus a Luxembourg EMI licence) whose app opens a multi-currency account and a Visa Platinum card (virtual and physical, both free), and throws in a data-only eSIM. How the benefit works: after KYC the app's eSIM section shows free data packs. Community reports through 2026 put it at 5GB a month for six consecutive months across 97 countries, exiting through a Singapore Singtel residential IP with a reputation score of 97, cleaner than a datacentre proxy, which suits services that only accept a Singapore IP. One October 2026 report got only two one-off packs of 1GB and 5GB instead, so the rules shift month to month and the app is the source of truth. The eSIM costs nothing and stays valid about ten years. It has no number, cannot receive SMS and is data-only; it can be written to a physical eUICC such as 9eSIM or Xesim for phones without eSIM support, and a new phone re-enables it in the app rather than claiming again. The bar is higher than most card accounts: a passport, an overseas address proof from the last 3-6 months (a statement) and a non-+86 phone number, with the address country matching the residence you pick. Machine review rejects address proofs often, and the community workaround is to resubmit the same photo once before switching documents. Review takes one to three business days.
Conditions
KYC needs a passport, an overseas address proof (a statement from the last 3-6 months whose country matches the residence selected) and a non-+86 phone number; the eSIM is data-only with no number and no SMS; the size and length of the free packs vary by account and campaign (5GB for six months, or a one-off 1GB plus 5GB); the same account also opens a free Visa virtual card funded with USDT, USDC or foreign currency.

What you get
eSIM.GG (known in Chinese communities as the turtle card) sells a prepaid eSIM with an Estonian +372 number. It is not a data-only travel plan: once installed it receives SMS, can call and take calls, and data can be bought per use. The number costs EUR 2.99 on the official site, there is no monthly fee, and the account balance does not expire. The keep-alive rule follows the official FAQ: any qualifying activity within 365 days, such as a little data, one SMS, one call, a top-up or a successful registration on a local network, restarts the 365-day window. After a full year without activity the number may be recycled. The vendor has announced a switch to a balance-change rule; until it lands, follow the site. Rates from the official coverage page updated 2026-11-21: data from EUR 0.88 per GB in most of Europe and Asia; a 10GB pack usable in 42 countries for EUR 9, covering China, the US, the UK, the EU, Malaysia and Thailand. Community tests in October 2026: total opening cost around CNY 30 (number plus a first balance), installed on an eSTK external card, and after about 24 hours the number received a WhatsApp verification code; Telegram codes also arrived on some number ranges (5405, 5406, 5311, 57, 59, 8103). Receiving SMS does not mean every platform accepts the number: the vendor explicitly does not guarantee third-party codes, and a new line needs about 24 hours of technical provisioning, so silence right after installation is not a setup error. Who it suits: people who want a low-cost foreign number that receives codes for years without a subscription. Who it does not: anyone who needs voice calls inside mainland China, or whose only requirement is one specific platform that must accept the number.

  4. Put the expiry date in a calendar and do one qualifying activity a month early each year
The EUR 2.99 does not include a first balance, so real opening cost is about CNY 30, and every year needs a small paid activity. The vendor has announced moving from activity-based to balance-based keep-alive, so the yearly cost must be recalculated once that lands. Third-party codes are not guaranteed and one working platform proves nothing for others. New lines need 24 hours to 3 days of provisioning. Voice is unavailable in mainland China and outgoing SMS costs EUR 0.24. The upstream operator can raise prices or shut the service down, with 90 days' notice at best.

≈$2

Deposit req.Buy the eSIM online at DITO's eShop or in the app, receive the QR code by email, install it and register in the DITO app to get a real +63 carrier number; PHP 99 includes 9GB for 15 days and a small top-up of about PHP 10-20 a year keeps the number, with community tests receiving SMS in mainland China

Ongoing ·A +63 carrier number, opened entirely online (order at the eShop, QR code by email, registration in the app); Philippine SIM Registration Act (RA 11934) applies and passport registration is required; mainland China SMS roaming works in community tests from November 2025 to August 2026 but is not an official promise OfficialOfficial
Global eSIM GuideDeposit req.Verified
Actual value≈$2 · PHP 99 incl. 9GB/15d
What you get
DITO is the Philippines' third carrier, and its prepaid eSIM is the cheapest option in the cloud-activated real-number category: order for PHP 99 in the official eShop or the DITO app, receive the eSIM QR code by email, scan it, complete registration in the DITO app and you have a +63 carrier number, not a VoIP number. The starter pack is not thin: 9GB of all-access data, unlimited texts to all networks, unlimited DITO-to-DITO voice and video calls and 150 minutes to other networks, valid 15 days. The first-year cost is therefore PHP 99, roughly CNY 12, with the number usable the same day. Keeping it alive works through top-ups: a Philippine prepaid card renews as long as there is a small top-up inside the validity window, and community guides budget one small load of PHP 10-20, about CNY 1.5-3, a year, through the DITO app or third-party channels. There is no official keep-alive package, so the lowest top-up tier shown in the app is the reference. Mainland China use is the point of this card: community reports record a number opened in November 2025 still receiving SMS in mainland China in August 2026, and receiving needs no data package - turn data roaming off and leave voice roaming on. Whether a message arrives still depends on the local network and sender, so this is a test result rather than an official promise. On verification codes and the barrier: a native carrier number passes ordinary SMS checks (WhatsApp, Telegram, cross-border e-commerce, some banks) far better than virtual numbers, though some platforms apply extra risk checks to Philippine ranges. Registration is the hard gate - the SIM Registration Act requires passport registration, foreign tourists usually also need a Philippine address and a return ticket, and a tourist SIM is legally limited to 30 days in principle. Being online longer does not erase that legal position, so do not make this the only recovery route for an important account.
Conditions
Buy online at the DITO eShop or in the DITO app from PHP 99 including 9GB for 15 days; complete Philippine SIM registration with a passport in the DITO app; under RA 11934 foreign tourists generally need a passport, a Philippine address and a return ticket, and a tourist SIM is limited to 30 days in principle; the phone must support eSIM and be unlocked; mainland China SMS reception is a community test, not an official commitment. Physical eUICCs such as 9eSIM V3 and Xesim are tested to write DITO successfully; passport registration in the DITO app and roaming activation are still required afterwards.

SoSIM is the prepaid brand of Hutchison Telecommunications Hong Kong (3HK) built around one card with two uses: new customers buy an eSIM for HK$33 on the SoSIM web store or in the WeChat mini programme, the QR code arrives at the verified email, and scanning it brings a real +852 number live in about ten minutes. The HK$33 choice: 50GB of full-speed Hong Kong data plus 1,500 local minutes for 30 days, or five days of Asia-Pacific roaming data covering Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand among 24 destinations plus 3GB of extra Hong Kong data for 30 days, switched in the account within 48 hours of activation. No contract and no admin fee. Keeping the number is the selling point: card validity, which is the number's validity, is separate from the starter package and starts at 120 days. New cards also get free conversion to eSIM and an HK$8 number change as standing offers, against a normal HK$28 conversion fee. SMS in mainland China: the official FAQ states the card works in any SoSIM roaming destination as long as there is roaming coverage, Wi-Fi is off and mobile data is on, so activation outside Hong Kong is possible. Hong Kong local service requires registration first, with a passport or a mainland travel permit and manual review of one to two hours, up to 48 hours; roaming-data-only use can skip registration. The official FAQ also states that once registered, SMS can be received free of charge abroad while the mainland data card is valid, so codes need no package. On verification codes: the +852 native carrier range works in tests for WhatsApp, Telegram, Hong Kong banks and brokers, Apple ID and WeChat, but many AI platforms including ChatGPT and Claude apply extra risk checks to Hong Kong ranges and often refuse them, which is where this card differs from a Philippine DITO number.

Global eSIM GuideFreeVerified
Actual value1GB of China roaming data plus an Austrian Drei +43 number (worth roughly $4)
What you get
The Telegram bot @roam_esim_bot works simply: send /checkin for one point a day and earn another point per invited friend, and five points buy an eSIM holding 1GB of data that roams in mainland China plus an Austrian +43 number. You can also buy one outright with /buy for 1 USDT, and /shop sells vanity numbers for 6 USDT. Note that the five-point free route nominally takes five days of check-ins, but stock drains fast enough that pure check-ins usually miss it, so most people get there by inviting one to three people who join and check in; without invites the only path is the 1 USDT purchase. Stock stood between 1,500 and 1,600 cards when it opened on the evening of 22 November and fell within hours as forums passed it around. Community tests (NodeSeek and the same thread on the Naixi forum) got a SIMlessly LPA that installs as a Drei eSIM, connected to China Unicom 4G inside China and showed the exit IP 91.223.100.36 in the United Kingdom. Someone redeemed one on the spot, so the flow does work. It is not, however, an official Roam product. The official Telegram channels listed on weroam.xyz/join_us are only @WeRoamXYZ and @WeRoamCN, plus official groups for Korea, Indonesia and Vietnam, and @roam_esim_bot is not among them. In other words a third party is reselling SIMlessly wholesale capacity through its own bot and borrowing the Roam name; the points, the stock, which profile gets issued and when the bot shuts down are all up to its operator. So treat it as a disposable test card: fine for checking eSIM compatibility, for emergency data or for one-off throwaway signups, but never put a bank, a payment app, your main mailbox or an important social account on that number.
Conditions
A Telegram account; join the channel and discussion group the bot names (about 30 seconds before it registers) before /checkin counts; one point per day plus one per invited friend (invitees must also join and check in); five points make a free card, but stock is consumed quickly, so five days of daily check-ins usually arrive too late and getting it free realistically means inviting one to three people; without invites the only route is /buy at 1 USDT (or /shop at 6 USDT for a vanity number); stock is limited and the rules can change or reset at any time.

Global eSIM GuideFreeVerified
Actual value500MB for 7 days (1 day or 100MB in some destinations, about $2)
What you get
Wanderly (Wanderly Technologies LLC, getwanderly.com) sells travel eSIMs and its paid catalogue covers 200+ countries and regions; the free trial does one thing, letting you test a small allowance before you fly. The allowance comes in three tiers: 500MB for 7 days (mainland China, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Thailand, Turkey, Australia, Vietnam, the US, the UK, Switzerland and 24 destinations in all), 500MB for 1 day (most of Europe plus Taiwan and Russia, 53 in all) and 100MB for 7 days (Canada, Brazil, Mexico, India, the UAE, the Philippines and 26 in all). On 23 November 2026 the official page listed 103 destinations. You can only claim it in the phone app; the website sells paid plans only. Install the app, create an account and the home tab shows the free-eSIM claim prompt. Pick one destination, check the allowance and validity, then complete the eligibility steps in the app. Wanderly states plainly that finishing verification does not approve a claim by itself, that the card check and the eligibility steps are separate, and that 500MB is not promised to everyone. One claim per account and one per device, ever, plus a daily cap on total claims. The card check is the part that matters. The official wording is that it is sometimes requested, and on the 500MB tier the field experience is that it does come up: you enter a card on a secure Stripe page and your bank confirms it. Nothing is charged and no subscription is created, so there is nothing to cancel afterwards. Wanderly keeps only the card type, issuing country and a protected card identifier to stop repeat claims, and never sees or stores the full number or security code. One piece of history is worth knowing: before 13 October 2026 the card check ran as a Zotlo $0 trial, and Wanderly says it has cancelled all of those. If zotlo.net or Z3P LLP turns up on a statement it is most likely from that period (Zotlo also bills for other companies, so match the order first). New purchases and card checks go through Stripe and appear as Wanderly Technologies LLC. The free plan is data only, with no number, so no calls or texts. The official line is that most plans start their validity when they first connect to a network at the destination, so install it at home over Wi-Fi and switch roaming on for that line after landing; this matters most on the 1-day tier. 500MB covers maps, ride-hailing and messages, and disappears quickly with video or cloud backups. Official pages do not say whether the free tier allows hotspot sharing; a third-party list says it does, so check it yourself.
Conditions
First-time Wanderly users only: one claim per account and one per device, ever, plus a daily cap on total claims; claimed only in the iOS or Android app, never on the website; the app may ask for a one-time card check (any bank card, entered on a Stripe page, no charge and no subscription), and passing it does not approve the claim by itself because the in-app eligibility steps still apply; one destination per claim, with the allowance (500MB or 100MB) and validity (1 or 7 days) set by what the app shows; an eSIM-capable, carrier-unlocked phone is required; data only, no number; the 1-day tier starts on first connection abroad and expires unused.

Actual value50 GB NVMe/6 GB RAM/200% shared CPU ($0)
What you get
Nodaroo is a small host that only launched in November 2026: nodaroo.com sells VPS, game servers, web hosting and app hosting, and lists locations in Frankfurt, Germany and Mumbai, India. On 22 November 2026 its free container appeared in Chinese communities: signing in to the free workspace at free.nodaroo.com with Discord gives one free container with 200% shared CPU, 6 GB RAM, 50 GB NVMe, a single server slot and a German node, with no card and no KYC. It matches the popular Altare on memory but offers five times the disk, so it spread fast overnight. Entry is Discord-only: the sign-in page has one button, "Sign in with Discord", and the OAuth scopes are identify, email and guilds.join, so signing in also joins their Discord server. Around 12:00 Beijing time on 23 November 2026 both the sign-in page and a public invite landing page still returned normally. The clean URL opens the base free plan; registering through someone's invite link adds 100 credits (the inviter gets 25), which can be spent on CPU, RAM, disk and slots, and this site publishes no invite links or codes, so use https://free.nodaroo.com/ directly. Their Discord lists limited-time upgrade tiers: Light (18 invites or 300 video views) moves to 24 GB RAM / 4 cores / 50 GB, Premium (25 or 600) to 32 GB / 6 cores / 50 GB, Extreme (35 or 1,000) to 48 GB / 8 cores / 80 GB. Technically this is not a bare KVM VPS with its own public IPv4 but a container panel. The front end is a Heliactyl-style panel and the host panel sits at panel.nodaroo.com (titled "Nodaroo Game Panel", a Pterodactyl panel), so there is no root and no native SSH: logs, files and commands go through the web console and SFTP (Pterodactyl's default port 2022), and only the ports the panel assigns to that container are open, with no arbitrary listening ports, no Docker inside and a 200% CPU allowance that is shared and throttled under fair use. Archive note (23 November 2026): the free tier started failing within a day. The user's own test on 23 November 2026 got "Something went wrong. Please retry or contact Nodaroo support" from the panel; the newest reply in NodeLoc thread t/topic/118974, at 11:44 Beijing time, read "It seems it's not working now.", and the thread's author had already reported that opening the China region errors out. Our requests from an overseas connection still returned 200 for the sign-in and invite pages around 12:00, but confirming that a container can actually be created requires a Discord sign-in, which would create an account and join their Discord, and we did not do that, so "it still works" is not verified; by decision this entry is archived with the specifications and panel details kept for reference.

Requesting the same path with GET falls back to the claim page, so the route now takes GET/HEAD only. The offer is therefore treated as dead and moved to the archive pending an official fix; neither easysim.ai nor the love.easysim.ai home page lists another claim entry point.
Conditions
[Since 2026-11-22 the claim endpoint returns 405 and the claim cannot be completed; archived] Install the EasySIM app and register with a phone number; one claim per phone number; limited quantity, ends when supplies do; the eligible countries and validity days are shown only on the in-app activation page.

Free trialArchived: on 2026-11-22 the official offer page already reads "Our free Network Trial has now ended" and no longer accepts London orders. The trial gave non-Vodafone customers a free 7-day Pay as you go Plus eSIM with 50GB of UK data, 500 UK minutes, 500 texts and a +44 UK number, with no number change or card needed; the community called it the festival eSIM, and the ordering device had to be located in London, which is where some users hit fraud checks. Ended Sep 30 ·London only: the device had to be located in London when ordering (the form was blocked anywhere else) and the trial worked in the UK only, with no roaming; new Vodafone customers only, and the email could not have been used for a Vodafone trial or account before SourceSource
Global eSIM GuideFree trialUnverified
Actual value≈$13 · 50GB + 500 min
What you get
Vodafone UK's "London's Best Network" 7-day network trial gave non-Vodafone customers a free Pay as you go Plus eSIM ordered online (or by scanning a QR code on the streets of London): 50GB of UK data, 500 UK minutes and 500 texts, valid for seven days counted from the day the order was completed (ending at 23:59 on day 7), with no number change, no card and no payment check, and the eSIM profile sent by email. Vodafone announced it in a press release on 6 May 2025 and said the same trial would travel to summer festivals including Glastonbury and Boardmasters, which is why the community called it the festival eSIM. NodeSeek and several activation guides shared it again around 2 August 2026, mainly for the +44 UK number that can receive verification texts. Requirements and risk controls: the device had to be located in London when ordering (the form was blocked anywhere else, and the 2026 terms also asked for a UK resident with a UK billing address); the contact number had to be a working UK number outside the Vodafone family (entering a VOXI or Vodafone number marked the user as an existing customer and failed); the postcode had to resolve to a London address; one trial per device, a daily order cap while supplies lasted, and the form only open between 08:00 and 22:00. Roaming was not allowed, so data, calls and texts worked in the UK only. Vodafone asked users to activate through the My Vodafone app, but the confirmation email carried the eSIM QR code, so it could be installed directly. The community warns that Vodafone UK bans device EIDs at a very high rate, which would stop that phone from activating any later Vodafone UK or VOXI eSIM, and advises a disposable blank eUICC instead. Archive note (22 November 2026): the official page (vodafone.co.uk/sim-only/pay-as-you-go-sim/London, now redirecting to /mobile/partnerships/network-trial-paygplus) has changed its heading and body to "Our free Network Trial has now ended" and only offers links to SIM only and phone deals, so the London trial no longer takes orders. Vodafone never published an exact end date; this entry records 30 September 2026 as its archive cut-off.
Conditions
[Archived: the trial has ended] The device had to be located in London when ordering and the form was blocked anywhere else; new Vodafone customers only, with an email never used for a Vodafone trial or account; one trial per device; the contact number could not be a VOXI or Vodafone number; an eSIM-capable, unlocked phone was required; the trial ran seven days, UK only, with no roaming; daily order caps applied while supplies lasted, and the form was open 08:00-22:00; activation was meant to go through the My Vodafone app (in practice the emailed QR code worked directly).
